sections.description: Introduces the engine block as the largest engine part, its role of housing cylinders, routing coolant and oil, and providing mounting points for accessories.
sections.title: Block basics and function

sections.description: Describes common block materials (cast iron and aluminium alloys), the move toward aluminium for weight savings, and mentions billet blocks used in high-end applications; notes the rough sand-cast surface and subsequent machining.
sections.title: Materials and manufacturing evolution

concepts: cast iron liners for wear resistance
sections.description: Explains how aluminium blocks handle cylinder bore either by directly machining cast iron bores or inserting/casting liners; discusses bonding into moulds and the role of liners in aluminium blocks.
sections.title: Cylinder liners in aluminium blocks and bonding

sections.description: Shows the importance of a smooth yet oil-retentive cylinder surface and introduces honing to create a fine crosshatch pattern that aids oil pooling for piston rings.
sections.title: Cylinder surface and finishing (honing overview)

sections.description: Defines the top surface (deck) and its mating to the cylinder head via a gasket; emphasizes the need for flatness and notes that multi-deck configurations require matched machining.
sections.title: Deck, head gasket, and multi-deck implications

concepts: lubrication routes to head and crank
sections.description: Outlines the internal oil passageways (galleries) and how oil is pumped from the sump, routed through the block, and distributed to the head and crank areas.
sections.title: Oil galleries and lubrication routing

sections.description: Discusses how lubrication works inside the block, including pressure regulation and the role of jets that spray oil to bearings and cylinder walls.
sections.title: Block lubrication overview and internal jets

sections.description: Demonstrates the installation of oil jets (one per cylinder), including locating pins, washer considerations, and hand-tight plus torque-wrench finalization.
sections.title: Installing oil jets

sections.description: Describes the crankshaft siting in the lower block area (crankcase), the five main caps, their circular bore requirements, and the importance of reinstalling them in the correct order.
sections.title: Crankcase, main caps and cap orientation

sections.description: Shows the sump/oil pan and a gasket/adhesive alternative for mounting on the underside of the block.
sections.title: Sump and gasket

sections.description: Explains core plugs (commonly called freeze plugs) used to remove sand from casts, their actual purpose, and notes that they can be a source of leaks if corroded or damaged.
sections.title: Core plugs and their purpose

sections.description: Covers engine mounting points to the block, including the mounting holes and the function of bosses and threaded surfaces for accessory attachments.
sections.title: Engine mounts and mounting bosses

sections.description: Discusses the rationale for circulating coolant around the cylinders to manage heat, prevent pre-ignition and excessive piston wear, and notes design goals to avoid air pockets and ensure proper flow.
sections.title: Coolant flow management and thermal considerations

summary: This video explains the engine block as the core structure that houses cylinders and supports accessories, detailing material choices (cast iron, aluminium alloys, and occasional billet blocks), manufacturing steps (casting vs. machining), cylinder preparation (liners, bonding/coatings, and honing), the critical flatness of the deck for a proper head gasket seal, the oil and cooling passages that service the engine, and essential assembly aspects (crankcase, main caps, sump, core plugs, engine mounts, and bosses). It also covers practical nuances such as the purpose of crosshatch honing, the difference between liners and coatings in aluminium blocks, the role of oil jets, and how coolant flow is designed to avoid air pockets and excessive piston wear. The narration blends theory with on-vehicle demonstration to connect block design to engine reliability and performance.
